newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pharming says owns no patents on PPL techno.
newsitem.headline: Pharming says owns no patents on PPL techno.

text.p: Unlisted Dutch biotechnology firm Pharming said on Monday that it held patents on the use of certain, but not all, DNA sequences to produce pharmaceuticals from the milk of transgenic mammals.

"The company has a broad patents position in the use of casein sequences (DNA) to produce pharmaceuticals from all transgenic mammals," said Rein Strijker, responsible for intellectual property ownership at the company.
But he said Pharming had not been issued with a patent on alternative DNA sequences such as those used by Britain's PPL.
Pharming was seeking to clear up confusion created by an earlier suggestion it owned the rights to all pharmaceuticals production based on milk from genetically modified mammals, Strijker said.
Pharming did however hold patents on the use of transgenic cattle as a platform for production of pharmaceuticals in milk, he said.
